note: The Duchy of Naxos (or Duchy of the Archipelago) was a Venetian-backed crusader state in the Cyclades Islands, created by Marco Sanudo (1207) after the Fourth Crusade. Sanudo, a Venetian nobleman, conquered the Cyclades and established a Latin duchy that would persist for over 350 years until Ottoman conquest (1579). The duchy was formally a fief of the Latin Empire of Constantinople; after 1261 it maintained autonomy by accepting Ottoman suzerainty while retaining Catholic Latin governance. The duchy's extraordinary longevity demonstrates Venetian skill in establishing durable island outposts.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Duchy of Naxos's 370-year persistence demonstrates the viability of island-based Crusader states outlasting mainland ones; the duchy's combination of Venetian commercial backing and Ottoman tributary status models the survival strategy that Ragusa also employed; the Cyclades under Latin rule preserve Catholic Christianity in an Orthodox-majority region
